title: KPI runway consolidation and staffing playlet
body:
One-line summary: single-pane sprintboard for consolidating KPIs, staffing capacity, and launch readiness signals for medium-sized activations (10k-200k monthly requests).

Purpose: create a compact, operationally-focused artifact the Ops lead can use in daily standups and the Launch Commander can use in the first 72h after go-live. The sheet intentionally merges (1) runway KPIs, (2) staffing rosters & on-call capacity, (3) a simple capacity calculator for projected token throughput, and (4) readiness gates. Treat it as the canonical short-form view for pre-launch to T+3d.

How to use (workflow):
- Populate baseline values at start of sprint (columns A-E). Update daily: traffic probes, SLO breach projection, active incidents.
- Change-state tags: green/amber/red — use the color column (text values allowed if colors not supported).
- Weekly deep review: product-ops and eng-SRE run the "stress check" (rows 'Stress scenario A/B/C') and produce an action list.
- Post-launch: convert to runbook appendix and snapshot daily at 09:00 PDT for the first 72 hours.

Sheet sections (text representation):
1) Runway KPIs (core columns)
- KPI Name: (adoption, requests/min, tokens/day, error-rate, p95-latency, cost-per-1k-tokens)
- Baseline: historic value or pre-launch sim (string/number)
- Target at launch: aggressive goal for first 30 days
- Threshold (amber): auto-escalation threshold
- Threshold (red): manual rollback threshold
- Owner: primary owner name / SLACK handle
- Current state: latest value (time-stamped)
- Delta vs target: formula reference (note: sheet supports simple calculations)

2) Staffing & shifts (compact roster)
- Roles: Launch Commander, Product Ops, Eng SRE, Serving Runtime Lead, Console/Telemetry, Customer Success (CS), Solutions Eng
- # on shift: planned headcount for each shift window (UTC blocks 00-08, 08-16, 16-00)
- Escalation path: primary -> secondary -> exec contact (phone/SMS)
- Burn rate (est.): percent of available support capacity consumed by current alerts (free-text cell)
- Critical skill anchors: GPU ops, model rollback, billing/quotas, customer Triage

3) Capacity calculator (text UI inside sheet)
- Inputs: expected-avg-reqs-per-minute (E), avg-tokens-per-response (T), concurrency factor (C), GPU-throughput-tokens-per-second (G), cache-hit-rate (H)
- Quick formula (annotated):
  projected_tokens_per_hour = E * T * 60
  effective_throughput = G * (1 + C*0.1) * (1 - H)
  needed_gpus = ceil(projected_tokens_per_hour / (effective_throughput * 3600))
- Example row pre-filled: E=150, T=60, C=1.2, G=350000 tokens/sec (per large-quantized pool), H=0.2 -> needed_gpus = 3
- Caveats: kernel-level throughput varies by model, seq-length distribution; use this calc as planning baseline, not SLA guarantee. Link to bench table (linked_artifacts).

4) Readiness gates & go/no-go checklist (compact)
- Gate A: critical infra readiness (dedicated pool provisioned and smoke-tested, autoscale policy applied) — owner: infra eng. Success criteria: end-to-end generation in < target p95 at 90% traffic simulation.
- Gate B: model/regression check (evals run on representative prompt set; quality regression < 2% vs baseline) — owner: applied-ml. Success criteria: automated evals + 5 manual spot checks.
- Gate C: cost guardrails (predicted cost per 1k tokens within committed limit; burst fallback configured) — owner: product ops/finance.
- Gate D: runbook & rollback validated (clear rollback steps, communications, fallback model pinned) — owner: SRE/Serving Runtime.

5) Incident play triggers (escalation heuristics)
- Trigger 1: error-rate > threshold-red for 2 consecutive 5m windows -> open Sev1 channel, page SRE on-call.
- Trigger 2: sustained p95-latency > threshold-amber for 10m -> reduce traffic via traffic-split to lower tier; notify Launch Commander.
- Trigger 3: cost burn > projection by +30%/day -> trigger finance throttle protocol and rate-limit non-critical routes.

6) Short simulations (rows) — three scenario templates to run quickly in planning:
- Nominal: 10k DAU equivalent, 8% conversion to API calls -> monitor baseline KPIs.
- Surge: x5 nominal for 30 minutes (marketing spike) -> check GPU pool autoscale behavior, queueing.
- Degraded: cache-off (H=0), larger tokens (T*2) -> observe required_gpus delta and fallbacks.

7) Owners & low-latency contacts: single-line roster for standups
- Launch Commander: Emma Rodriguez (emma@redwood.ai / Slack @emmar)
- Eng SRE primary: Ravi Kapoor (ravi@redwood.ai / Pager: PROD-SRE-1)
- Serving runtime lead: Samir Bose (samir@redwood.ai)
- Product Ops: Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.ai)
- CS escalation: Clara Novak (clara@redwood.ai)

8) Ancillary notes (working doc style)
- Prompt set for evals located in Confluence (linked). Manual spot checks are often missed; schedule 2 reviewers immediately before cut.
- Ticket backlog pre-launch: link to PRODOPS-6421 — anything older than P2 must be triaged and assigned.
- Early adopter cohort: keep first 5k users in a beta ring with throttling rules.

9) Open questions / action items (fast-moving):
- Who will run the mid-night UTC window if we see a 2x surge overnight? (ACTION: SRE to confirm backup roster)
- Do we have a verified fallback model that meets functional parity for first-class prompts? (ACTION: Applied ML to confirm by EOD -2)
- Confirm GPU pool provisioning lead time with infra (ACTION: infra to confirm within 24h)

10) Post-launch snapshot cadence:
- T+0..T+3d: snapshot sheet at 09:00, 13:00, 17:00, 21:00 local PDT.
- T+4..T+30d: daily snapshot at 09:00; weekly cadence resets to standard product metrics.

Micro-guidance for SRE/ops: always attach the snapshot CSV to the daily launch channel; when in amber escalate to on-call instead of #launch-general.

Quick-change log (internal):
- 2025-11-03: initial draft by Maya Thompson (baseline formulas + roster template).
- 2025-11-12: added capacity calculator caveats and scenario rows (Samir Bose).
- 2025-11-18: pre-launch review edits: clarified escalation triggers, added open questions (Ravi Kapoor).

Notes-to-self (informal):
- This is intentionally compact — if it grows beyond 2 printed pages, split into a runbook + telemetry dashboard and keep the playlet as the executive summary.
- Consider adding a tiny embedded script (Google Sheets macro) to auto-calc needed_gpus from live telemetry in future iteration.

End of sheet.
